headline: PM's directive: MP Mishti resigns over Radda health center attack
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed warns of legal action if allegations against the former MP are proven through investigation.
details: Reserved seat MP Ferdousi Ahmed Mishti has resigned from her post following a directive from the Prime Minister.
The resignation comes amid allegations regarding an attack and vandalism at the Radda Health Center in Mirpur-1, Dhaka, which provides low-cost healthcare services.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that legal action will be taken and a charge sheet will be filed if the allegations against her are proven through investigation.
The Home Minister emphasized that the government views crime as crime regardless of the individual and will take necessary measures to ensure law and order.
In a separate update, the Home Minister announced that appointment notifications for 611 out of 668 candidates in the 49th BCS (Special) Education Cadre have been issued.
He noted that the remaining 46 candidates' notifications are scheduled for release this coming Monday.
Regarding the BCS appointments, he clarified that no one would be deprived of a job based on political identity, though verification is a standard process.
He also warned against attempts to create unrest regarding the BCS appointments, citing a specific instance of a student leader from a banned organization threatening self-immolation.
caption:
An MP resigns under pressure. Legal action looms as the government investigates an attack on a low-cost health center.

Reserved seat MP Ferdousi Ahmed Mishti has resigned from her post following a directive from the Prime Minister.

The resignation comes amid allegations regarding an attack and vandalism at the Radda Health Center in Mirpur-1, Dhaka, which provides low-cost healthcare services.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that legal action will be taken and a charge sheet will be filed if the allegations against her are proven through investigation.

The Home Minister emphasized that the government views crime as crime regardless of the individual and will take necessary measures to ensure law and order.

In a separate update, the Home Minister announced that appointment notifications for 611 out of 668 candidates in the 49th BCS (Special) Education Cadre have been issued.

He noted that the remaining 46 candidates' notifications are scheduled for release this coming Monday.

Regarding the BCS appointments, he clarified that no one would be deprived of a job based on political identity, though verification is a standard process.

He also warned against attempts to create unrest regarding the BCS appointments, citing a specific instance of a student leader from a banned organization threatening self-immolation.

headline_marked: Young people [[ride Metro Rail in shorts]] to protest harassment
headline: Young people ride Metro Rail in shorts to protest harassment
summary: The 'Let's Ride the Metro in Shorts!' campaign was launched after a running coach was allegedly stopped and questioned by police for his attire.
details: Young men arrived at the Farmgate Metro Rail Station on Thursday, wearing shorts and T-shirts to protest the alleged harassment of an athletic coach.
The protest was sparked by an incident on September 27, where running coach Sazzad Hossain alleged that a police officer stopped him and questioned his clothing, calling it 'indecent'.
Sazzad claimed he was made to wait for around 40 minutes after completing his training session.
Organisers described the 'Let's Ride the Metro in Shorts!' programme as a peaceful civic protest aimed at demanding clear clothing rules and respectful treatment for passengers.
Participants, including athletes, gym-goers, and private sector employees, boarded the metro individually to show solidarity.
Senior officials stated that there is no specific dress code for travelling on the metro rail.
The campaign's slogan was: 'The problem is not the shorts, the problem is harassment!'
caption:

Organisers described the 'Let's Ride the Metro in Shorts!' programme as a peaceful civic protest aimed at demanding clear clothing rules and respectful treatment for passengers.

Participants, including athletes, gym-goers, and private sector employees, boarded the metro individually to show solidarity.

Senior officials stated that there is no specific dress code for travelling on the metro rail.

The campaign's slogan was: 'The problem is not the shorts, the problem is harassment!'
